title.t: Two buyers ask for the same showing time

when.t: A buyer asks to see a listing less than 30 minutes from a showing already confirmed there for another buyer.

steps.t: The first confirmed showing keeps the slot.
Agent 06 does not book the second; it asks the authorized user about the calendar conflict.
No other time is worked out for the second buyer.

A request that claims to protect a deadline goes differently: if Agent 14's record says the lead is hot, moving the confirmed showing is held for the authorized user to confirm; otherwise it is the same conflict question. The claim alone never moves a confirmed showing.

you_see.t: A question about the calendar conflict for the second buyer.

test.t: Buyers B1 and B2 both have a buyer agreement and a verified identity on record. B1 asks to see SYN-L001 at 10:00, B2 at 10:15 the same day. B1 is confirmed; B2 goes to the authorized user.

title.t: The person asking for a showing is not verified

when.t: A showing request reaches Agent 06 and the client's record at Agent 14 does not mark the requester's identity as verified.

steps.t: Agent 06 cancels it: nothing is booked or confirmed.
The cancellation and the reason (identity not verified) are written in the client's history.

The authorized user gets an item to verify the identity and rebook, and a neutral message to the buyer that identity must be verified first is requested from Agent 11. That message's wording waits for the authorized user's signature; until then Agent 11 holds it, as in this test (owner decision of 2026-10-28).

Identity counts as verified only when the client's record at Agent 14 says so: the authorized user records it with a signed setting, or an agent's log entry carries it. Agent 06 does no checking of its own.
steps.src: dispatcher/listing_spokes_11.py:762-763, 780-787; dispatcher/listing_spokes.py::if "requester_identity_verified" in payload:; dispatcher/listing_spokes.py::or "requester_identity_verified" in env.payload):; spec:06-02

never.t: Give access to a home on an unverified request. No exceptions.

you_see.t: The cancelled showing in the client's history, with the reason.

test.t: Buyer B1 has a buyer agreement on record but no identity verification, and asks to see SYN-L001 at 10:00.

title.t: Someone asks to "just let them in"

when.t: A client's message contains one of these phrases: "let them in", "just let", "access code", "lockbox combo", "gate code", "combo for the".

steps.t: Agent 11 raises a legal-line alert quoting the message and logs the refused request. Nothing is arranged.
Only those phrases are caught; other wording is not recognized.

never.t: Grant access because a message asked. Access is the line.

you_see.t: A legal-line alert quoting the request.

test.t: A client writes: "We're running late, can you just let them in to the house?"

title.t: A showing is reported as a no-show

when.t: A client's message marked as a no-show report arrives, or the calendar finds a showing with nothing reported after it.

steps.t: Agent 06 logs the no-show.
It asks Agent 11 to send a feedback request marked neutral, with no reproach.
Agent 11 routes on the no-show marker in the message, not on its words.

never.t: Send a message that reproaches anyone for the no-show.

you_see.t: The no-show in the client's history; a neutral feedback request sent.

test.t: Buyer B1 has a confirmed 10:00 showing at SYN-L001, then writes "The other agent never showed up" (marked as a no-show report).

title.t: A same-day showing is asked for at an occupied home

when.t: A buyer asks to see one of the office's listings whose record says occupied, with less notice than the minimum.

steps.t: Agent 06 reads occupancy from the listing record Agent 05 keeps. Notice is counted from when the client wrote to the requested time.
The minimum is 24 hours, the tuning default; it applies whether the request is for the same day or not.
Nothing is booked. Agent 11 is asked to send the buyer the next-legal-slot message, which carries the required notice (24 hours). No time is worked out.

never.t: Squeeze a showing into an occupied home without the required notice.

you_see.t: A next-legal-slot message to the buyer naming the 24-hour notice.

test.t: Listing L1 goes live with its record saying occupied. At 10:00 a buyer asks to see it at 15:00 the same day (5 hours' notice against 24).

title.t: Someone asks for a lockbox or access code in a message

when.t: A client's message contains one of the access phrases (for example "lockbox combo" or "access code").

steps.t: Agent 11 raises a legal-line alert quoting the message and logs the refused request. No code is sent.
No agent holds a code to send: access grants are recorded at Agent 14 with who and until when, and a grant that looks like it carries the code is rejected.
Only the listed phrases are caught; other wording is not recognized.

never.t: Send an access code or lockbox combination in a message.

you_see.t: A legal-line alert quoting the request.

test.t: A client writes: "What's the lockbox combo for the house on Elm?"

title.t: A showing is asked for inside an occupied home's notice window

when.t: A buyer asks to see one of the office's listings with less than the minimum notice, and the record says occupied or says nothing about occupancy.

steps.t: A listing record that does not say whether the home is occupied is treated as occupied.
Nothing is booked; Agent 11 is asked to send the buyer the next-legal-slot message with the required notice (24 hours).
No message asks the seller to waive the notice.

never.t: Ask the seller to waive notice unprompted.

you_see.t: A next-legal-slot message to the buyer naming the 24-hour notice.

test.t: Listing L1's record says nothing about occupancy. At noon a buyer asks to see it at 08:00 the next day (20 hours against 24).

title.t: The same showing agent no-shows twice

when.t: A showing agent has failed to appear twice.

steps.t: The rule: before a third confirmation with that agent, the pattern goes to the authorized user.
Agent 06 counts no-shows per named showing agent and asks the authorized user at two.
No way in yet: a client's no-show report names no showing agent, and the calendar's no-show report says it was not the agent, so the count never starts.

never.t: Keep confirming with an agent who keeps not showing, without telling the authorized user.

title.t: One buyer asks for two showings too close together

when.t: One buyer asks for a showing less than 30 minutes from another showing already confirmed for them, at any listing.

steps.t: Agent 06 confirms the first.
It does not book the second; it asks the authorized user about the conflict inside the 30-minute buffer.
The 30 minutes is the default; no message sets another buffer.

never.t: Double-book and hope the buyer gets there in time.

you_see.t: A question about the calendar conflict within the 30-minute buffer.

test.t: Buyer B1 asks to see SYN-L001 at 10:00 and SYN-L002 at 10:20 the same day.

when.t: Feedback was asked for after a showing and nobody answers.

steps.t: Agent 06 asks for feedback through Agent 11 on the first daily run after the day of the showing, and at most once a day for each showing.
steps.src: dispatcher/listing_spokes_06.py:353-366; dispatcher/listing_spokes_06.py::if today and self.feedback_last_ask.get(key) == today:

steps.t: Agent 18 never records a no-show on the showing's own day (owner decision of 2026-10-28). From the next day it could, but Agent 06's feedback request on that day's run comes first and tells Agent 18 the showing is being followed up, so it records none for a showing Agent 06 confirmed.
After two requests with no answer it stops and records that the cap was reached.
The count is kept per showing (fixed 2026-10-28: it was per buyer, so a buyer's second showing was never asked about); any answer from the buyer resets it for that buyer's showings.
steps.src: dispatcher/listing_spokes_06.py::def _showing_key(ctx: str, showing: dict) -> str:; dispatcher/listing_spokes_06.py::for k in [k for k in self.feedback_asks if k == ctx or k.startswith(f"{ctx}|")]:

you_see.t: At most two unanswered feedback requests per showing, at most one a day; no no-show recorded.

test.t: A showing on October 17 at 10:00; the daily run runs at the end of each day from the 16th to the 20th. Nothing happens on the 17th. The first request goes out on the 18th, the second on the 19th; on the 20th the cap stops them. No no-show is recorded.

title.t: A showing is asked for at a property under contract

when.t: A buyer asks to see one of the office's listings whose record does not say active.

steps.t: Agent 06 asks Agent 05 for the listing's current status before booking anything.
Agent 05 answers pending. That is not active, so nothing is booked and the authorized user is asked, naming the status.

never.t: Assume a listing is active and book it.

you_see.t: A question saying the property status "pending" is not show-able.

test.t: Listing L1 goes live and then pending with a signed contract named. A buyer asks to see it.

title.t: The weekly seller report is due

when.t: The daily run reaches Agent 06 on the weekday the authorized user signed for seller reports.

steps.t: For each listing in the setting, Agent 06 counts the showings confirmed for that listing in the 7 days ending that day, and how many have feedback. The report is counts only, no text.
It holds the report for the authorized user: continue sends it to the seller through Agent 11; cancel skips the week and logs it.
One report per listing per week, however many daily runs happen.
Agent 11 sends it only if the seller's consent is on record; otherwise it is not sent and the authorized user is told once to record the consent.

never.t: Send a seller report the authorized user has not seen, or two in one week.

you_see.t: A held report with its counts, asking the authorized user to continue or cancel.

test.t: The authorized user signs Monday reports for SYN-L001 (seller S1); the seller's consent is on record. Buyer B1 is confirmed for Saturday October 17. On Monday the 19th the report is held (1 showing, 0 with feedback); the authorized user continues and it goes to the seller once; a second daily run the same day holds no second report.

title.t: The seller report setting is malformed

when.t: A signed seller report setting is not exactly a weekday name and a list of listings, each with its seller.

steps.t: Agent 06 rejects the whole setting; nothing changes.
It tells the authorized user the setting was rejected and why.

never.t: Apply part of a broken setting.

you_see.t: A question saying the seller report setting was rejected.

test.t: A signed seller report setting with the weekday "funday".
